recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future work should only revisit wording if OO wants broader narrative examples for group-based nutrition orders; the conformance source already implements the requested reference choice.
issue_request: FHIR-20508 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and asked whether NutritionOrder can be used for groups in veterinary and research settings; the final resolution was to add Group as a reference choice for the former patient reference.
initial_application: No commit in this checkout explicitly mentions FHIR-20508. The requested change appears to have been applied implicitly by commit 1a5062f0a41dca024be7fb527908dcec638166f8, which changed NutritionOrder.patient to NutritionOrder.subject, broadened the definition to a person or set of individuals, added Group as a target profile, added a subject search parameter, and rewired the legacy patient search to NutritionOrder.subject.where(resolve() is Patient).
additional_context: NutritionOrder is an active current-build resource in source/fhir.ini. The current source retains the R4/R5 rename mapping from NutritionOrder.patient to NutritionOrder.subject, so the Jira wording about patient.reference maps to the current subject element. A later Applied issue, FHIR-41411, treats group-supported nutrition subjects as established background while expanding group support for other nutrition-family actor positions. Zulip and Confluence searches found no contrary or narrower community decision for FHIR-20508.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The authoritative current source already allows NutritionOrder.subject to reference both Patient and Group, and the search parameter source supports the current subject search while preserving the legacy patient search constrained to Patient.

related_jiras.note: Later nutrition-family issue states Nutrition already supports Group as a subject and adds Group to other nutrition actor positions, supporting rather than changing this decision.
